name: DCM Shriram Ltd
title: DCM Shriram Ltd - 523367 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: DCM Shriram Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 9% to INR3,564 crore and PBDIT 12% to INR364 crore; reported PAT of INR693 crore includes INR474 crore one-time tax credit.
summary.overview: Consolidated net revenue grew 9% YoY to INR3,564 crore and PBDIT rose 12% to INR364 crore, led by Chemicals (revenue +33%, PBDIT +24%). Vinyl PBDIT nearly doubled on price gains despite a 25% fall in PVC volumes, while Bioseed swung to a loss on delayed monsoon. Reported PAT of INR693 crore includes a INR474 crore one-time tax adjustment and INR79 crore of other one-time gains; underlying PAT was INR147 crore, up 28%. Management flagged weak rural demand, soft Q2 vinyl offtake and a 15-20% Kharif sowing shortfall as near-term headwinds.

financial_highlights.change: Includes INR474 crore one-time tax adjustment and INR79 crore one-time gains
vs INR236 crore a year ago

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue +33% YoY and PBDIT +24% to INR274 crore; ECU prices firmed 7% with caustic volumes flat. Capacity utilisation 82% for caustic, ~85% for hydrogen peroxide, ~70% each for epichlorohydrin and epoxy.

segments.name: Vinyl
segments.commentary: Revenue -10% YoY on PVC volumes -25% despite prices +22%; utilisation 100% vs 98%. PBDIT +88% to INR43 crore; carbide volumes and prices each +15%.

segments.name: Sugar and Ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue -2% YoY; domestic sugar volumes -8%, realisations +2%. PBDIT INR22 crore vs negative INR7 crore last year, which included a ~INR36 crore one-time ethanol duty provision. Sugar inventory 20.8 lakh quintals vs 27.7 lakh a year ago.

segments.name: Fenesta Building Systems
segments.commentary: Revenue +22% YoY; PBDIT +13% to INR40 crore, diluted by product mix and fixed costs for new platforms. Order book up 4%, roughly INR1,000 crore.

segments.name: Shriram Farm Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue +2% to INR357 crore; PBDIT +22% to INR30 crore on better margins in crop protection and specialty plant nutrition despite muted volumes.

segments.name: Fertilizer (Urea)
segments.commentary: Revenue +11% with realisations +19% and flat volumes; PBDIT fell to INR23 crore from INR38 crore, as the year-ago quarter had a INR24 crore one-time gain.

segments.name: Bioseed
segments.commentary: Revenue -26% YoY; PBDIT negative INR9 crore vs INR42 crore last year on lower corn and paddy volumes and weaker cotton margins.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give forward caustic price guidance, but said ECU is just below INR30,000/t and expects prices in that range or higher; chlorine is at minus INR7,000 to minus INR8,000/t.
Bharuch aluminium chloride and calcium chloride projects expected to start commercial production in Q2 FY27.

Kota 68 MW peak hybrid renewable project under commissioning, with average injection of 25 MW in July; Serentica 58 MW hybrid agreement signed to take peak renewable capacity at Bharuch and Kota to about 176 MW.
Cash tax outgo expected at about 19% for at least five years through MAT credit utilisation of INR376 crore, while P&L tax rate stays at 25%.
Net borrowings at FY27 end expected to be similar to current levels, with a reduction of about INR200 crore possible; capex of about INR1,000 crore planned this year.
Demolition of the group demerger: application to government targeted within FY27, timeline uncertain.
Vinyl demand expected soft in Q2 FY27; government reinstated basic customs duty on PVC imports and DGFT set minimum import price of US$766/t for six months.
Bioseed: large part of Kharif volume lost; no firm recovery guided for Q2.
capex_capacity: Caustic soda utilisation 82% in Q1; expected to improve as downstream projects commission. New flaker facility lets part of caustic output be exported.
Epichlorohydrin and epoxy plants running at ~70% utilisation with ramp-up ongoing; epoxy plant in Gujarat acquired October 2025.
Grain-based ethanol capacity can be run up to 260 KLD; management said it does not plan to add ethanol capacity.
Chlorine: after current projects, ~50% captively consumed; with pipeline and regional customer tie-ups, ~85% tied up.
Fenesta setting up a wooden door manufacturing facility; two acquisitions worth ~INR450 crore completed in the 12 months to June 2026.
demand_pricing: Domestic caustic demand steady from alumina, soaps and detergents, and textiles; hydrogen peroxide oversupplied in Asia.
PVC: imports surged after temporary customs duty waiver and Chinese imports; offtake weak on labour shortages, heatwave and cautious buying.
Sugar: global deficit of ~0.7 mt expected in 2026-27; domestic sugar price around INR4,450/quintal, expected to stay firm for a couple of months.
Ethanol: installed capacity ~2,000 crore litres vs OMC allocation ~1,060 crore litres; sugarcane feedstock only 28%.
Kharif sowing shortfall of 15-20% all-India and much higher in Bioseed markets; rainfall patchy after July.
Urea: subsidy regime governed by FICC; management says government is paying domestic makers on time, and gas-price spikes are a pass-through.
Fenesta order intake only up 4%; management attributes slowdown to customers deferring decisions amid West Asia crisis.

qa_highlights.question: Caustic soda price outlook for the near term and FY27, and current chlorine price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it normally avoids forward price statements, but noted ECU is just below INR30,000/t and expects that level or higher. Chlorine is at minus INR7,000 to minus INR8,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: Why is SFS profitability up on flat top line, and how will Kharif profitability shape up if monsoon holds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited farmer reach, new R&D products and market credibility. It said monsoon has been good only in pockets, sowing is 15-20% lower, and it cannot project Aug-Sep outcomes.

qa_highlights.question: Will more capacity be diverted to grain ethanol given better sugar prices, and how is ethanol profitability set to move?
qa_highlights.answer: Grain-based ethanol can run up to 260 KLD and will be optimised for margins, which are currently good on maize. Management said it does not plan to add capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR400-odd crore tax reversal and the cash tax impact going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: It relates to a six-year ITAT-backed position, with MAT credit of INR376 crore. P&L tax stays at 25%, but cash tax outgo is about 19% for at least five years.

qa_highlights.question: Crushing outlook for next season and sugar price expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to call next year's cane harvest given the monsoon. Sugar prices, around INR40-50/kg per the analyst, are expected to stay firm for the next couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for urea margins given global price spikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Urea pricing is governed by FICC rules, so international prices do not hit domestic makers. Government is paying on time; gas price spikes are a pass-through that can strain cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise and what is the year-end net borrowing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt did not rise in Q1; the comparison is year-on-year, covering about INR450 crore of acquisitions and about INR1,000 crore of capex. Year-end net borrowing should be similar, with about INR200 crore reduction possible; debt/EBITDA is kept below 1.5x, with AA+ rating.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the group demerger and expected Bioseed recovery in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is committed to the demerger and aims to file the application with government in FY27, with no firm timeline. Bioseed: large part of Kharif volume is lost and no firm recovery was guided for Q2.

risks_watch: Kharif sowing shortfall of 15-20% all-India, with much higher gaps in Bioseed markets; August-September rainfall under El Nino is the swing factor for SFS, Bioseed and rural demand.
Vinyl: soft Q2 offtake, PVC import surge after the temporary duty waiver, and whether reinstated basic customs duty and US$766/t minimum import price support domestic prices.

Caustic and chlorine: ECU near INR30,000/t and chlorine at minus INR7,000 to minus INR8,000/t; caustic utilisation at 82% depends on downstream commissioning, including Bharuch aluminium and calcium chloride in Q2 FY27.
Reported PAT of INR693 crore is inflated by INR474 crore one-time tax and INR79 crore other gains; underlying PAT is INR147 crore, so track the MAT-driven cash tax rate of about 19%.
Fenesta order book up only 4% (about INR1,000 crore), attributed to customers deferring decisions amid the West Asia crisis; margins diluted by new platforms.
Leverage: net debt INR1,649 crore vs INR1,481 crore a year ago, with about INR1,000 crore capex and possible LNG-driven rise in fertilizer subsidy receivables (INR292 crore at 30 June 2026).
key_quotes: So, we normally do not make forward-looking statements, but we do expect the prices; current ECU is in the range of just below INR30,000.
So effectively for, you know, let's say anywhere between 5 to 10 years, at least 5 I can see in the foreseeable future, my effective tax rate will be 19% or tax outgo will be 19%.
And yes, there will be some reduction by about INR200-odd crore probably, but it will all depend how the sugar season pans out, how much will be the inventory.
Our R&D focus is now the key issue which is going to be a major driver going forward, where there is a lot of stress from the management's side.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and balance sheet, but cautious and often non-committal on near-term prices, monsoon, Bioseed recovery and demerger timing. Management declined forward price and sugar cane-harvest guidance, citing unpredictable external factors.
